questions.question: State any three uses of the data visualization tool. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• State any three uses of the data visualization tool.
  • Data visualization tools are used to turn raw data into clear, actionable insights across many
  • fields.
  • • Used in business intelligence and decision-making- Tools like Tableau and
  • Microsoft Power BI help organizations track performance through dashboards,
  • revealing trends in sales, customer behaviour, and operations
  • • Used for data exploration and analysis - Instead of scanning spread sheets, analysts
  • use visuals to uncover hidden patterns, correlations, and anomalies
  • • In communication and reporting, visualizations make findings easier to present to
  • stakeholders
  • • Real-time monitoring. - Many industries rely on live dashboards to track systems,
  • such as website traffic, financial markets, or supply chains. Visual alerts and trend
  • lines allow quick responses to changes or issues.
  • • Public policy and governance- visualizations help communicate data like population
  • trends, economic indicators, or health statistics to the public.
  • • Used in marketing and customer analytics

questions.question: Discuss three examples of geographical data used in real life. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss three examples of geographical data used in real life.
  • Geographical data refers to data that represents the location shape and characteristics of
  • features on earth’s surface
  • • Navigation and route planning
  • Apps like Google Maps use geographical data such as road networks, traffic
  • conditions, and user location to suggest the fastest routes and estimate travel time.
  • • Weather forecasting
  • Meteorological departments use geographic data like latitude, altitude, and satellite
  • imagery to predict weather patterns
  • • Urban planning and smart cities
  • City planners use geographical data to design roads, public transport, drainage
  • systems, and zoning areas. Population density maps and land-use maps help decide
  • where to build schools, hospitals, or parks.
  • • Disaster management
  • During floods, earthquakes, or landslides, geographic data helps identify high-risk
  • zones and plan evacuation routes.
  • • Agriculture
  • Farmers and agricultural agencies use data on soil type, rainfall, and land elevation to
  • decide which crops to grow and when to plant or harvest
  • • Transportation and logistics
  • Delivery services use geographic data for route optimization, tracking shipments, and
  • reducing fuel costs. GPS systems help companies manage fleets efficiently.
